prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on any string argument whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, so a valid string that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "null", "[1,2]") gets silently corrupted for any union type that includes `str`, most commonly `str | None`. Both PRs patch pre_parse_json to detect such str-containing unions and skip the JSON parse. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py calls json.loads() on any string argument whose field annotation isn't exactly `str`, so a valid string that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "null", "[1,2]") gets silently corrupted for any union type that includes `str`, most commonly `str | None`. Both PRs patch pre_parse_json to detect such str-containing unions and skip the JSON parse. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both change pre_parse_json to stop coercing string values for str-containing unions, but they cover different cases. #3056 calls _unwrap_annotated() on each union member before checking it, so it correctly recognizes the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern used throughout this SDK for documented optional-string parameters. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead tests raw type identity against a frozenset {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}; `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` is not a member of that frozenset, so its `any(arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES ...)` check still returns True and pre_parse_json keeps attempting json.loads on Annotated-described optional strings — leaving the reported corruption bug unfixed for that common case. #2032's frozenset approach does additionally cover non-str simple-type unions like `str | int` or `str | bool` that #3056 deliberately leaves untouched (per its own docstring, scoped only to str | None). Since Annotated+Field is the standard style for described tool parameters in this codebase, #3056's handling is the more load-bearing fix for the actual reported issue.

prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id both route through `_request_streams` keyed by the id, letting the second request overwrite the first's slot and cross-wire responses in StreamableHTTP's `_handle_post_request`. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id both route through `_request_streams` keyed by the id, letting the second request overwrite the first's slot and cross-wire responses in StreamableHTTP's `_handle_post_request`. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 rejects duplicates by checking `request_id in self._request_streams` where the key is `str(message.id)`; this collapses JSON-RPC integer id `1` and string id `"1"` into the same key, so it can falsely 400 a distinct-typed id or still cross-wire responses in that case, and it doesn't guard a string id equal to the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel. #3221 replaces the bare `str(id)` key with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (`i:`/`s:` prefixed) applied consistently to both `_request_streams` and the event store, closing the int/str collision and the GET_STREAM_KEY collision that #3063's simpler check leaves open.

clusters.pick_reason: Both change pre_parse_json to stop coercing string values for str-containing unions, but they cover different cases. #3056 calls _unwrap_annotated() on each union member before checking it, so it correctly recognizes the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern used throughout this SDK for documented optional-string parameters. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead tests raw type identity against a frozenset {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}; `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` is not a member of that frozenset, so its `any(arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES ...)` check still returns True and pre_parse_json keeps attempting json.loads on Annotated-described optional strings — leaving the reported corruption bug unfixed for that common case. #2032's frozenset approach does additionally cover non-str simple-type unions like `str | int` or `str | bool` that #3056 deliberately leaves untouched (per its own docstring, scoped only to str | None). Since Annotated+Field is the standard style for described tool parameters in this codebase, #3056's handling is the more load-bearing fix for the actual reported issue.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 rejects duplicates by checking `request_id in self._request_streams` where the key is `str(message.id)`; this collapses JSON-RPC integer id `1` and string id `"1"` into the same key, so it can falsely 400 a distinct-typed id or still cross-wire responses in that case, and it doesn't guard a string id equal to the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel. #3221 replaces the bare `str(id)` key with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (`i:`/`s:` prefixed) applied consistently to both `_request_streams` and the event store, closing the int/str collision and the GET_STREAM_KEY collision that #3063's simpler check leaves open.

clusters.pick_reason: Both change pre_parse_json to stop coercing string values for str-containing unions, but they cover different cases. #3056 calls _unwrap_annotated() on each union member before checking it, so it correctly recognizes the idiomatic `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` pattern used throughout this SDK for documented optional-string parameters. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json instead tests raw type identity against a frozenset {str, int, float, bool, NoneType}; `Annotated[str, Field(...)]` is not a member of that frozenset, so its `any(arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES ...)` check still returns True and pre_parse_json keeps attempting json.loads on Annotated-described optional strings — leaving the reported corruption bug unfixed for that common case. #2032's frozenset approach does additionally cover non-str simple-type unions like `str | int` or `str | bool` that #3056 deliberately leaves untouched (per its own docstring, scoped only to str | None). Since Annotated+Field is the standard style for described tool parameters in this codebase, #3056's handling is the more load-bearing fix for the actual reported issue.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 rejects duplicates by checking `request_id in self._request_streams` where the key is `str(message.id)`; this collapses JSON-RPC integer id `1` and string id `"1"` into the same key, so it can falsely 400 a distinct-typed id or still cross-wire responses in that case, and it doesn't guard a string id equal to the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel. #3221 replaces the bare `str(id)` key with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (`i:`/`s:` prefixed) applied consistently to both `_request_streams` and the event store, closing the int/str collision and the GET_STREAM_KEY collision that #3063's simpler check leaves open.
